summary: Single-author four-arm ablation on the DABStep text-to-SQL/analytics benchmark across four models. It separates a 'context layer' into semantic prose content, retrieval scaffolding (nine governed tools plus allow-lists), and pre-computed views, using a YAML data contract that can be 'hollowed' (prose emptied) or compiled to views. Main finding: semantic content does most of the work, delivering it via one-lookup tools beats pasting the same manual into the prompt, and declared forbidden operations stopped all mutating SQL.

claims.claim: Content delivered through the contract raises hard-task accuracy from 13.9/22.6/22.9/37.0% (bare schema) to 55.1/56.6/68.4/77.4% on four models.
claims.evidence: Table 4 hard column matches the abstract exactly; Table 5 schema-vs-contract McNemar p from 2e-15 to 1e-35. Hard-split golds are reconstructed and run ~3-6pp lenient (§4.4, §8.4).

claims.claim: Scaffolding without content is worth 0-5 points on flash models and 14-15 on frontier models; content outweighs scaffolding by 1.8x-6.6x.
claims.evidence: Table 4 schema vs hollow hard: GLM 13.9->19.3, DeepSeek 22.6->22.6, Sonnet 5 22.9->38.0, GPT-5.6 37.0->51.2; Table 5 last row p=0.058/0.61 (flash) vs 9e-9/4e-7 (frontier). Single run per model; the frontier/flash split rests on two models each and was not predicted (§8.3).

claims.claim: The contract beats the same knowledge pasted into the prompt because the rule is one lookup away.
claims.evidence: Table 4 manual vs contract hard: +32.2, +13.7, +44.6, +27.1pp; §6.1 SQL carries all six fee clauses 39/65/55/98% vs 3/9/4/4% for prompt arm. Confound acknowledged in §8.2: the contract adds seven INTERPRETATION clauses that resolve ambiguities the manual leaves open (reversing one changes answers on 87/97 payment tasks); the fifth arm needed to separate them was not run. Manual arm beats contract on easy tasks on all four models.

claims.claim: Declared rules deterred mutation: ungoverned arms issued 166 mutating statements, governed arms none.
claims.evidence: §7, Table 10 (e.g., GLM schema 27, manual 92, governed 0); the validator never fired, so deterrence came from declared rules in context, not enforcement.

claims.claim: On one model the benchmark's withheld golds grade contract 51.9% vs 18.8% for the prompt baseline.
claims.evidence: §4.4: GLM all-450 sweeps submitted to the leaderboard; 378 hard tasks; McNemar p=4.9e-28. Independent grading for one model only.

patterns.note: Fetch-one-rule-at-a-time contract beats the same knowledge pasted into a 24,000-character prompt on all four models (hard split).
A pasted domain manual (analogous to a large instruction file) was indistinguishable from bare schema on Sonnet 5 hard tasks; structured, retrievable content worked much better.
Declared forbidden operations plus table allow-list: 166 -> 0 mutating statements; enforcement layer never needed to fire.
Machine-readable data contract (semantics + rules) as the agent's source of truth.
Nine governed tools expose the warehouse; the paper shows the tool surface alone (hollow arm) adds little on flash models.
Per-arm cost reported; contract arm is the cheapest per correct answer on three of four models.

methodology.sample: DABStep 401 of 450 tasks with reconstructed golds (332 hard, 69 easy); DeepSeek complete-case 279 tasks after 29% loss to rate limits; 6,416 transcripts.
methodology.baselines: Bare schema, hollow contract, manual pasted into prompt (practitioner baseline), compiled-view ceiling. No external text-to-SQL systems compared beyond leaderboard band checks.
methodology.models: glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, Claude Sonnet 5, gpt-5.6-sol; medium reasoning effort; temperature 0 only on the two flash models.
methodology.variance: No repeats. One near-replicate on GLM shows a 23.4% per-task flip rate at temperature 0 (§8.3). Paired exact McNemar, Wilson CIs, 24 tests with no multiplicity correction.
methodology.ablations: Four-arm ladder is itself the ablation; missing fifth arm (contract minus interpretation clauses).
methodology.contamination_controls: None run; DABStep is public. Author argues memorisation would not depend on context arm (an inference, §8.5).

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; no venue in comment or journal_ref.
standards.artifacts: Harness, frozen and hollow contracts, raw rows and all 6,416 transcripts with SHA-256 digests at github.com/flyersworder/agentic-data-contracts (release dabstep-eval-2026-09).
standards.preregistration: Text refers to a pre-registered design and records departures (primary model substituted, Sonnet 5 added late, those contrasts labelled exploratory); no registry link found in the text.

biases.detail: Author wrote the contract (including the interpretation clauses that resolve manual ambiguities) and the open-source library under test; the hollowing design partly mitigates.
Each model run once; observed 23.4% per-task flip rate between near-identical GLM runs.
One benchmark, one domain: 294 of 332 hard tasks are fee questions; 450 tasks collapse to 113 question shapes (§8.1).
Capability-trend claims rest on two flash and two frontier models that disagree on some contrasts.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Author's own open-source agentic-data-contracts library is the instrument; commercial models evaluated neutrally.
coi.detail: No commercial vendor tie; intellectual self-interest in the library and the contract approach. The leaderboard-graded GLM contrast provides a partial external check.

verdict_reason: A careful decomposition: the abstract numbers match Table 4, the threats section is candid, one contrast is graded officially, and transcripts are fully released. However, there is a single run per model, one benchmark and domain, and the contract-vs-prompt margin is confounded by interpretation clauses that the author added to the contract only.
applicability: Strong design signal for the Java ingestion team even though the domain is analytics SQL. (1) Put healthcare-education content semantics (field meanings, licensing/audience rules, versioning conventions) into a machine-readable, versioned contract that agents fetch rule-by-rule through a tool. Do not paste long docs into AGENTS.md or the prompt. (2) Write the semantics before building retrieval tooling or pre-computed helpers. (3) Declared forbidden operations and allow-lists in the contract cut destructive actions to zero, which matters for ingestion jobs touching shared stores. For ≥4 ingestion repos, a shared contract artifact could serve as the cross-repo SoT and fits spec-driven development. Caveats: the tool layer is a Python library; host-agnostic delivery would be via MCP or CLI. Results came from analytics questions, not code changes in Java services. Gains held only inside the contract's domain.

conflicts_with.detail: That ablation finds AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md context strategy does not move coding-agent correctness; here curated semantic content raises accuracy by 26-45 points. The difference is consistent with domain semantics that agents cannot infer (fee rules) vs repository knowledge agents can discover.
Agreement rather than conflict: both find compact authoritative metadata is the largest single lever and that unstated contract details masquerade as model error.
